Subject: Stellar Order Form v2 - TF/C & Auto-renew

Hi Ben,

Thanks for the demo — the product looks promising. Our procurement and legal teams reviewed the draft Order Form and the attached redline (Stellar_OrderForm_v2_redline.pdf). Two items block approval on our side:

1) Termination for Convenience (TFC): the current MSA language allows Redwood to terminate for convenience with a 30-day notice. We cannot accept a unilateral short window; we need either mutual TFC or a longer notice period (we prefer mutual with 60 days).

2) Auto-renew / Notice window: the Order Form states auto-renew with a 30-day opt-out notice. Given our procurement cycle we need a 120-day opt-out window or an annual rollover that requires explicit renewal for large TCV deals.

I've attached our suggested Order Form redline. Can your team propose a middle ground? Procurement is willing to accept a mutual TFC at 60 days if Redwood can accommodate a 90–120 day auto-renew notice for the initial term only.

If helpful we can do a short call with legal this week.

Thanks,
Natalie Chen
Head of Procurement — Stellar Data

Short reply from my side: we can engage legal and procurement internally and propose a compromise. My suggested pathway:
- Offer mutual TFC with a 60-day notice (commercially reasonable).
- Offer a 90-day auto-renew opt-out as our standard compromise; allow 120 days for exec-approved deals or higher TCV.
- Add a one-time migration grace period (30 days) during initial offboarding to avoid interruptions.

Marissa / Karthik / Laura — can legal/procurement review and prepare a clean redline and a short rationale we can present back to Stellar? If we agree, I'll set a short 30-minute call with Natalie + Stellar legal.

Forwarding Ben's thread. Internal take and proposed redline approach below — attaching a doc with proposed MSA edits (MSA_redline_changes.docx).

Key points for legal to prepare:
- Make TFC mutual and set notice to 60 days; include a short list of excluded items (prepaid credits, one-off migration fees).
- Auto-renew: propose 90-day opt-out as our baseline; allow 120-day opt-out for deals with TCV > $500k or where customer requests and execs approve. Record the exec approval path in the order form ("requires Director-level approval").
- Add an initial-term carveout: for the initial 12-month term only, Stellar may request a one-time 120-day notice; after that, 90-day notice applies. This is a commercial concession to get the deal live faster.
- Add migration grace clause: 30 calendar days of transitional access at no charge, subject to return of customer data / handoff plan.
- Add equitable termination assistance language: data export / escrow obligations during offboarding.

Please prepare a clean redline and a 1-pager justification we can share with Natalie. Karthik, please flag any regulatory or security showstoppers.

Marissa Cole
VP, Deals & Legal Operations — Redwood Inference

Those concessions look reasonable — but two asks from our side before we sign off: 
1) We need the 120-day opt-out to be available as an option (not just for >$500k), but capped to one exercise within the first 12 months (one-time exception).
2) We need explicit language around notice receipt (email to contracts@stellardata.com) and a minimum service continuity guarantee until the end of the notice period (no accelerated termination during the notice).

If you can confirm those two items in your redline, we can route to Stellar's GC for a final pass and get DocuSign ready. I've re-attached our Order Form redline for reference.

Thanks — happy to jump on a 20-min call if needed.

Best,
